text:
sam: quick UX check: new metrics panel has req/s + p95(ms). I prototyped an 'interactive axis' control that lets users drag the top of the y-axis to reveal spikes. thoughts?
prit: interesting. that avoids dual axes but adds a control that might be hidden. need affordance.
anu: love the idea if it's discoverable. maybe show a tiny handle icon on hover + keyboard control.
maya: accessibility: interactive handles must be keyboard operable and have aria-labels like 'Increase Y max' / 'Restore auto scale'.
sam: UX tradeoff: when you drag to expand, do we rescale both series proportionally or only the active series?
prit: prefer rescaling whole chart to keep visual alignment. but we should add a per-series "focus" toggle to dim others.
anu: outliers: propose a 'spike drawer'—collapsed vertical gutter that summarizes clipped spike counts; clicking opens raw values. keeps main canvas stable.
maya: name is cute. copy for drawer tooltip: "X spikes hidden. Click to open raw values." keep short.
sam: smoothing: offer two modes — rolling median (robust) and exponential (responsive). default median for ops dashboards. document in tooltip.
prit: legend: add unit microcopy inline (visual: • req/s, • ms). SR should read full words. legend items also get a small control to 'focus' series.
anu: short SR text suggestion: "Chart shows throughput (requests per second) and 95th percentile latency (milliseconds). Use keyboard to expand y-axis or open spike drawer for raw values."
maya: engineering note: implement handle with role='slider' and step small integer, and spike drawer accessible via button with aria-expanded.
design-bot: summary: "Interactive axis handle + keyboard support; spike drawer for clipped outliers; rolling median default smoothing; legend units visible and SR-friendly; per-series focus toggle."
sam: thanks. @prit will mock the handle affordance, @anu will draft SR copy, @maya will add a11y implementation notes.
